text:
sam: Starting the infra apply for release/2026-03. Change window open now (2h). Primary goal: roll out the TF IAM policy cleanup + vpc route tweak. Pinning provider: aws = \"~> 4.35\" for this run. Please stand by for deploy-bot plan.
deploy-bot: [2310001235] queued terraform plan (branch=release/2026-03, workspace=prod). Serial apply slot allocated (az-serial=3).

deploy-bot: plan started...
```
Refreshing Terraform state in backend: s3://redwood-tf/prod
module.iam.aws_iam_role.app: Refreshing state... [id=redwood-app]
Error: aws_iam_role.app: role has changed since last apply (diff in assume_role_policy)
```
mira: seeing the same in canary (us-west-2). Canaries failing healthcheck after bind change. Not a global breaker yet but noisy.

kelly: which exact diff? full policy or just a principal? if it's only microprincipal we might be able to patch without full rollback.

mira: looks like we removed a cross-account principal that the metrics agent uses. deploys in us-west-2 lost metrics write perms -> service-level alerts.

aj: pinging infra-oncall. Suggest we do a scoped rollback: revert the IAM module to commit sha abc123 for prod only, keep VPC route change staged. That avoids full-service rollback.

sam: agree. emergency plan: rollback iam module in prod canary region then monitor for 10m. If healthy, continue staggered apply. Update release notes to reflect pivot.

kelly: propose exact commands to run so deploy-bot can execute safely. I'm +1 on targeted revert.

sam: OK roll with the following and handoff to deploy-bot.
```
# emergency revert: target only iam module in prod/us-west-2
git checkout abc123 -- modules/iam
terraform apply -target=module.iam -var 'region=us-west-2' -auto-approve
```
deploy-bot: received rollback job. queued as high-priority (serial slot preempt if needed). Will run with plan + apply:target.

deploy-bot: [2310001248] starting apply -target=module.iam in us-west-2 (operator=sam).
```
Apply complete: 1 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed
Outputs: iam_reverted = true
```
oncall-ops: canaries green in us-west-2 after 90s, metrics infra back online. No customer-facing incidents observed. Monitoring: increased 1xx auth failures resolved.

aj: we should also pin the aws provider in the root module to avoid implicit upgrades causing assume_role diffs. I'll open a quick PR to enforce provider ~>4.35 and add a provider lockfile entry.

sam: good. Also add a release-note snippet: \"Reverted IAM policy change in prod canary to restore agent cross-account access; VPC route change delayed to next window.\"

kelly: let's add a follow-up to run an eval against internal metrics to ensure no regressions next 24h. I'll add an alert mute for the rollout window.

mira: for the postmortem, I'd like to capture why the assume_role diff wasn't caught in preflight checks. Maybe expand evals to include service account access tests.

sam: agreed. We'll do a short blameless postmortem and link PRs. Thanks all for quick turnaround :thumbsup:
